questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
First and foremost, I wanted to try living in a different country and having my daily life there. Due to the Covid-19 situation, I had to choose a destination in Europe for this. I have always enjoyed traveling to Italy due to the culture, the people and the food, and on top of this the Covid situation there seemed to be rather stable.  

Secondly, I wanted to go on exchange to further challenge myself academically. Going to Italy made sense for me, since they too are a part of the EU and allow for the choice of EU-related courses. 

Thirdly, I wanted to go to a country in which I could travel around. Italy is great for this. There are many beautiful places to explore and traveling around is not that expensive.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall it was an enjoyable experience. While I will not rate it higher than 8, I still would not change my past decision of going on exchange to Italy. Going on exchange is definitely something I believe everyone should experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. The university in Milan has a very poor website for orientation and their physical offices can be confusing to navigate. They respond and do in fact help you, if you contact them per mail, but generally I found it quite frustrating, that I could not easily find answers to my questions or worries. On the plus side, bureaucracy does not really exist in Italy, so even if you miss a deadline or forget something, they fix it for you either way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. I had to find it myself on their website and/or go physically to their offices to pick up my student card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Whilst I only rate it as a 1, there is not really that much to do upon arrival except for sending the university information about insurance and picking up your student card. A good trick is to getting in contact with other erasmus students and hoping they can explain or help you with it. That is how I figured out how to access the online student portal and my student mail.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was quite easy, but me and the two other students I found housing with where early birds in this matter. We found housing 2 months before departure to Italy, which proved to be a very smart thing to do. 

If you look for off campus housing, beware of scammers!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Beware of scammers. Find housing in good time. Housing off campus is quite expensive, don't be surprised if you  end up paying +700€ monthly. Be creative, look for housing through various sites like airbnb, "roomie" or similar. Avoid facebook groups, they seem to be full of scammers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found my place through airbnb. Simply contacted the landlord directly and asked for the option of leasing the apartment for 5 months, which he agreed to. Small and not perfect, but all in all a cozy apartment.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration was not that difficult. You simply do this through their website. The only issue was, that while registering for courses, you could not see when these courses take place. You had to find the schedules for the individual courses on a different link, which I was not aware of before signing up. However, it was not a problem to have courses overlapping with each other.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As stated above, you log into the "Unimia" student portal and choose the courses you wish to register for and press accept. You have to write the course information in manually, but the process is quite simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Whilst the registration proces is simple, it does not contain much useful information, meaning information about the various courses has to be found in different places on the university website. Some of this information is "public", and some of this information you cannot access without logging in to the student portal.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the courses I had applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and figure out whether or not the courses overlap with each other. It can be annoying to have classes during the same hours, since "attendance" matters for the final exam. Do not worry about the exam dates, you have the option of attending each exam in each course in December, January and february - choice is yours.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This is a tricky question, because some of the courses I followed were extremely well structured, inspiring and the professors were good. Other courses were confusing and it was hard to understand, what the aim of the teachings were in relation to the exam.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the courses was quite varying. In some courses the professors simply expected us to know stuff, which some had never heard about before, and in other courses they explained the contents and teachings as if it was middle school. 

While this is said, I do not believe the level was in any way hard, and passing is easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is very different, but this is also what makes it fun to try. Attendance is not at thing at UCPH, while it definitely is in Italy. You cannot simply skip too many classes. The style of teaching is also different and the professors expect you to participate and answer their questions. Most professors do not expect you to, but it matters for the overall grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
M&A: The contract
European Monetary Law
Competition law and economics
Smart cities, artificial intelligence and digital transformation law
Negotiation, mediation and sustainable conflict resolution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Competition law and economics 
M&A the contract

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any large ones as far as I remember. I did however spent unexpectedly a lot on traveling, going out and shopping.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Drinks were more expensive compared to other italian cities. 
Transportation by train is also expensive if you plan on traveling a lot. 
Food is quite cheap and so is coffee.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Non-existant. There are some sports club but they are not promoted to Erasmus students at all.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
None except for a volleyball team which not many exchange students were a part of. 
The beginning of the semester included some social activities thanks to ESN (Erasmus Student Network), but compared to the many other universities in Milan, the social activities at UniMi were not great. Find your own group of friends and plan your own social stuff! This is not so hard

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Travel! Cities like Bologna, Parma and Venezia are not far from Milan. Flying to Sicily is also not that expensive. Go to other parts of Italy, visit museums and go out and have nice food and drinks. 
Lots of opportunities to watch sports such as Football. If you go in the Autumn semester you can go watch Formula1 in Monza.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spend time with the people you meet here. Go out town with them to have a good time, be cultural or to travel. Do not worry too much about the studies; passing is easy and you do not need to study too much for the individual classes. Have a good time while it lasts.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not that hard. Especially if you arrive a week or two before the actual semester starts. I think its a subjective question, but I would not say it is hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for various whatsapp groups and try and make friends in that way. You can ask if anyone wants to go out and have a drink or see X or Y place together. Participate in the ESN social events and be outgoing. You can also make good friends through the classes you attend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language. If you do not speak italian, it can be hard to communicate in some places. You will manage though. I do not speak any Italian, and I did not find it challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the drinks. And the beauty of the country in nature, history and architecture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go some time before the semester starts to settle in your own tempo. It makes the start less stressful
2) Try and make friends through WhatsApp groups for exchange students. These can be found by asking around or through the big "erasmus milan" facebook group. 
3) Use the time here to relax, enjoy yourself and generally just have a good time. Sure, there are exams to pass and stuff to study, but make the best of your time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have covered most of this in my previous answers.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships you make and the fact that you get to exit your "normal" routine back home to live a new, temporary life in a different country (with amazing food and drinks).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Deciding to do all my exams in the month of December. I do not regret this, but it was tough to have 3 exams in 3 days.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No. I think my above answers cover the exchange period well :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
